appraisal_events.evidence: je la remerciai avec exagération... afin qu'une autre fois elle m'obéît de même pour telle ou telle chose; j'ajoutai ces paroles mensongères... Ainsi échangeâmes-nous des paroles menteuses.
appraisal_events.explanation: The in-scene narrator deliberately overpraises and manipulates Albertine to secure her future obedience, staging himself as the one exerting emotional control in the exchange; the narrating voice immediately flags this and her reply as mutual lies, undercutting any straightforward self-elevation.

status_effects.explanation: By strategically flattering and mildly deceiving Albertine to condition her future compliance, the in-scene narrator gains local emotional leverage in the relationship, though the passage's framing of the whole exchange as mutual lying keeps this gain uncertain rather than clearly triumphant.

ambiguities: Scoring le narrateur here is delicate: his manipulative rhetoric toward Albertine mirrors and produces the accepted E1 diminishment of her, but the passage explicitly labels the entire exchange as 'paroles menteuses' on both sides, so it is uncertain whether the narrator is being locally elevated in emotional leverage or whether the narration is quietly deflating his own account of control.

Andrée, Françoise, M. Verdurin, and Mme Verdurin were considered but omitted: Andrée is a bare mention (riding companion) with no evaluative content; the Verdurins appear only as the object of Albertine's already-scored renunciation with no distinct outcome of their own; Françoise is a functional messenger figure and, in the later dream passage, a figure the narrator's essayistic reflection merges with his own consciousness rather than stages as a social participant.
